Candidates:
[note:wiki/decisions/sync-conflicts.md] Sync conflict resolution: When both sides changed the same note, keep both; the remote version is saved as a copy named '<title> (conflict <date>)' in Inbox. Notes changed on only one side are taken as is. This decision covers note bodies and titles; it says nothing about tags, which at the time lived in the note body. A follow-up was planned to extend the rule to metadata once tags had their own storage. Conflict copies inherit the remote note's metadata as it was when the conflict was detected.

On sync, tag sets are merged per note as a union of both sides, with removals tracked as tombstones for 30 days. A note created offline sends its tags in the same batch as its body; if the batch is split, tags are applied after the note exists. Conflict copies get the tag set of the version they were copied from, and a tag tombstone never removes a tag from a conflict copy. The merge runs on the server inside the same transaction as the body merge, and its tests live in merge/tags.test.ts.

Batches are capped at 200 changes; larger queues are split into several batches sent in order. Candidates:
[note:wiki/decisions/visibility-timeout-v2.md] Visibility timeout v2: Timeout is per queue, default 30 s; workers extend the lease every timeout/3 while a job runs. This governs running jobs only. Jobs that have not started yet are not affected by lease extension.
[note:wiki/decisions/delayed-jobs.md] Delayed and scheduled jobs: Decision: a delayed job is stored with an absolute visible_at computed by the broker from its own clock at enqueue time. Workers never compute visibility; they only poll the broker, which compares visible_at against the broker clock. Producer clocks are ignored. Broker hosts must run time sync; a drift alarm fires above 500 ms. Rationale: computing visibility on producers or workers made delays depend on whichever host's clock was furthest off, which caused early and late firing in 2025. With a single broker clock, the only drift that matters is the broker's own. If several broker nodes serve one queue, visible_at is compared on the node that owns the queue partition, so partition moves between nodes with different clocks can still shift timing.
